source.title: Lifted Representation Hypothesis in Language Models

record.tranche_reason: The study tests a lifted-state account of generalization and revision, but does not test superposition, feature competition for capacity, SAE feature recovery, or the dimensionality of superposed features. It discusses superposition as background for possible neural implementations.
record.gate_note: The paper reports behavioral generalization and revision results and measures type-conditioned MLP activation similarity. These concern lifted-state organization, not the feature overlap, capacity competition, sparse-feature recovery, or feature dimensionality named by the claim versions. The paper's discussion of superposition and candidate neural bases is conceptual, and cited findings are not results of this study.
record.test_reason: The study tests a lifted-state account of generalization and revision on a modulo-rule task. Its activation analysis measures type-conditioned MLP activation distances, not feature superposition, capacity competition, polysemanticity, SAE recovery or feature dimensionality. Superposition and SAEs appear only as cited candidate neural bases in the appendix.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that across full fine-tuning, LoRA and ICL, models generalize the broad rule to the withheld subtype but fail to localize its later revision, degrading the parent group G2 more than the control G5. They call this behavioral evidence consistent with the Lifted State Hypothesis and say identifying the latent states needs representational and causal analysis.
record.recipe_differences: The paper does not reproduce or apply the Toy Models of Superposition method; it studies sequential generalization and revision and proposes a lifted-state account.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported relative activation patterns vary by model, layer, and training stage; the paper also reports effects of update method and context ordering in its separate behavioral task.

fits_no_version.finding: During W1, the share of cross-control pairs farther apart than the Type 2–Type 4 pair rises in both Qwen and both Gemma models; Llama starts high and largely maintains it. The advantage drops after W2 begins in all five models, with model-specific layer patterns (Fig. 12–13).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In fine-tuned LLMs, a held-out subtype's MLP activation pattern becomes selectively close to its trained parent type relative to control types. This closeness weakens when the subtype receives conflicting supervision.

record.problems: The authors state that the experiments provide behavioral rather than direct representational evidence for lifted states. The activation similarity analyses use a controlled synthetic task and five seeds; plotted values are not transcribed in the text. The paper also notes that behavioral comparisons do not uniquely identify the latent type or rule underlying the activation patterns.
record.rows_left_out: No rows for the behavioral generalization/revision outcomes: those measure task performance and interference, not any of the listed superposition or polysemanticity versions. No rows for discussion or cited evidence about neurons, sparse features, or superposition because those are not results of this study.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity sweeps or feature geometry.
No measure of neuron polysemanticity or capacity competition.
No measure of polysemanticity or its causes.
No feature-spreading measure across neurons and no SAE. The MLP activation-distance analysis concerns type grouping, not sparse features.
No SAE features are trained or evaluated.
Not tested. The paper says lifted states need not be one-dimensional, but this is a conceptual statement only.

record.verdict_notes: The rows are correctly linked to none. For R2, R4, R6, R8 and R10, 'observed' refers to the paper's own effect (a decrease after W2), not to any superposition version. The paper mentions superposition (Elhage et al. 2022) and SAEs only as candidate implementations, which is background citation.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test toy-model feature storage, sparsity-dependent transitions, or superposition geometry.
Does not test whether neuron polysemanticity results from competition for limited representational capacity.
Does not test whether polysemanticity can arise without capacity pressure.
Does not identify features spread across neurons or features recovered by an SAE; type-conditioned neuron activation similarity is not a feature-spreading or SAE-recovery test.
Does not test SAE feature completeness, stability, or canonical status.
Does not test whether superposed features are one-dimensional directions or multidimensional features.
